incidente.resumo: A dashboard bug caused repeated, unnecessary calls to the Tenant Service API; together with a Tenant Service update this overwhelmed the service, and because it is part of API request authorization, many APIs and the Cloudflare Dashboard failed. Adding resources and rate limiting helped but were insufficient; availability returned to 100% after the problematic Tenant Service change was reverted.

descricao.texto: An increase in API usage was seen; the team noticed increased usage across the Tenant Service.
trechos: We immediately saw an increase in our API usage but found it difficult to identify which requests were retries vs new requests.
In this case we noticed increased usage across our Tenant Service, so we focused on reducing the load and increasing the available resources.

descricao.texto: A bug in a new dashboard version caused repeated, unnecessary calls to the Tenant Service API: a problematic object included in a React useEffect hook's dependency array was recreated on every state or prop change, so the useEffect re-ran each time and the API call executed many times during a single dashboard render instead of once.
trechos: The incident’s impact stemmed from several issues, but the immediate trigger was a bug in the dashboard. This bug caused repeated, unnecessary calls to the Tenant Service API.
The API calls were managed by a React useEffect hook, but we mistakenly included a problematic object in its dependency array.
Because this object was recreated on every state or prop change, React treated it as “always new,” causing the useEffect to re-run each time.
As a result, the API call executed many times during a single dashboard render instead of just once.
A new version of the Cloudflare Dashboard is released which contains a bug that will trigger many more calls to the /organizations endpoint, including retries in the event of failure.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: The dashboard behavior coincided with a service update to the Tenant Service API, compounding instability and ultimately overwhelming the service, which then failed to recover.
trechos: This behavior coincided with a service update to the Tenant Service API, compounding instability and ultimately overwhelming the service, which then failed to recover.
2025-09-12 17:50 | A new version of the Tenant API Service is deployed.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: The Tenant Service is part of the API request authorization logic; without it authorization cannot be evaluated and API requests return 5xx status codes, so its overload impacted other APIs and the dashboard.
trechos: When the Tenant Service became overloaded, it had an impact on other APIs and the dashboard because Tenant Service is part of our API request authorization logic.
Without Tenant Service, API request authorization can not be evaluated. When authorization evaluation fails, API requests return 5xx status codes.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: The Tenant Service was not allocated sufficient capacity to handle spikes in load like this.
trechos: Finally, the Tenant Service was not allocated sufficient capacity to handle spikes in load like this.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: When the Tenant Service was restarted, every dashboard began to re-authenticate with the API at once (a thundering herd), making the API unstable again; this was amplified by the dashboard bug.
trechos: When we restarted the Tenant Service, everyone’s dashboard began to re-authenticate with the API. This caused the API to become unstable again causing issues with everyone’s dashboard.
This pattern is a common one often referred to as a Thundering Herd.
This is common, but was amplified by the bug in our dashboard logic.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: It was difficult to tell retries from new requests, which made it harder to identify the issue as a loop in the dashboard.
trechos: We immediately saw an increase in our API usage but found it difficult to identify which requests were retries vs new requests.
Had we known that we were seeing a sustained large volume of new requests, it would have made it easier to identify the issue as a loop in the dashboard.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: The Tenant Service had not yet been migrated to Argo Rollouts, which automatically rolls back on detected errors; the authors state it would have automatically rolled back the second Tenant Service update, limiting the second outage.
trechos: We use Argo Rollouts for releasing, which monitors deployments for errors and automatically rolls back that service on a detected error.

We’ve been migrating our services over to Argo Rollouts but have not yet updated the Tenant Service to use it. Had it been in place, we would have automatically rolled back the second Tenant Service update limiting the second outage.
